quote: After it had been contested several days, it was at last resolved, that peace should neither be granted nor refused.
notes: Aetolian ambassadors supplicate the senate for peace; after days of contested debate the senate dictates harsh alternatives and orders them out of Italy (livy:en:37:1).

quote: Publius Scipio Africanus said, that if they decreed that province to his brother, Lucius Scipio, he would go along with him, as his lieutenant-general
notes: Consuls Laelius and L. Scipio both contest the Greek command until Africanus's offer to serve as legate swings the senate to his brother (livy:en:37:1); coded as electoral-conflict for command-assignment dispute.

quote: that the fleet was going off to a distance from Ephesus, from the war which concerned themselves
notes: Discontented talk among the military tribunes over the Patara expedition reaches and sways the praetor Aemilius, who turns the fleet back to Samos (livy:en:37:17); grumbling that shaped command, not an actual mutiny.

quote: the answer given to Antiochus was, that they could not treat of peace before the arrival of the consul
notes: Antiochus's first peace overture is debated in Aemilius's council at Elaea, where Eumenes argues no treaty is valid without consul, senate, and people (livy:en:37:19).

quote: But rage and avarice were too strong for his authority
notes: Roman soldiers plunder surrendered Phocaea against the praetor's explicit orders, and Aemilius can only salvage his pledge by protecting free persons in the forum (livy:en:37:32); army-politics breakdown of command.

quote: These concessions, which appeared to the ambassador of great moment towards obtaining a peace, the Romans deemed trifling
notes: Antiochus's envoy Heraclides offers terms in full council and privately tries to bribe Africanus with gold and his captive son, but the Romans demand cession beyond Taurus and talks collapse (quote at livy:en:37:35; bribe attempt in 37:36).

quote: Resign all pretensions in Europe, and cede that part of Asia which lies on this side of Mount Taurus
notes: After Magnesia, Antiochus's envoys accept whatever terms the Romans dictate; Africanus delivers the conditions in council at Sardis and the matter is referred to ambassadors at Rome (livy:en:37:45).

quote: the senate refused a triumph to Minucius, but, with great unanimity, decreed one to Acilius
notes: Rival triumph claims from returning proconsuls are decided by the senate, which denies Minucius and grants Acilius a triumph over Antiochus and the Aetolians (livy:en:37:46); coded electoral-conflict as closest type for a contested honors grant.

quote: the senate decreed, that Caius Laelius, the consul, if he thought proper, should enrol six thousand families, to be distributed among these colonies
notes: Deputies of Placentia and Cremona complain of depopulation and the senate decrees six thousand supplementary colonist families with commissioners to conduct them (livy:en:37:46).

quote: Marcus Aemilius Lepidus sought the office under general censure, for having, in order to sue for the office, left his province of Sicily
notes: Hotly contested consular election in which Lepidus canvasses under censure for leaving Sicily without leave and is rejected when Fulvius, elected alone, names Manlius colleague (livy:en:37:47).

quote: that the Aetolian ambassadors should be ordered to leave the city that day, and to quit Italy within fifteen days
notes: A second Aetolian embassy offends the senate with insolent recitals of past services and is expelled from Rome and Italy by decree on Acilius's motion (livy:en:37:49).

quote: At last religion prevailed, so that the flamen obeyed the order of the pontiff; and the fines were remitted by order of the people
notes: The chief pontiff detains the flamen-praetor Fabius Pictor from his Sardinian province, producing stormy deadlock in senate and before the commons with fines, tribunician appeals, and an attempted abdication (livy:en:37:51); veto-deadlock is the nearest type for this inter-magistrate jurisdictional standoff.

quote: The senate voted, that the peace should be observed; and the people, a few days after, ordered it
notes: After hearing Eumenes, Smyrna, the Rhodians, and Antiochus's envoys, senate and people ratify Scipio's peace and appoint ten commissioners to apportion Asia (livy:en:37:55; hearings span 37:52-56).

quote: Lucius Valerius Flaccus, Marcus Atilius Serranus, and Lucius Valerius Tappo, triumvirs, settled a Latin colony at Bononia, according to a decree of the senate
notes: Triumvirs plant a Latin colony of three thousand at Bononia on land confiscated from the Boian Gauls, with graded allotments for horsemen and other colonists (livy:en:37:57).

quote: commenced a prosecution against him, on a charge, that he had neither exhibited in his triumph, nor lodged in the treasury, a large part of the royal treasure
notes: Tribunes prosecute the censorial front-runner Glabrio for embezzling Antiochene booty, with Cato's testimony decisive, until Glabrio withdraws his candidacy and the tribunes drop the fine (livy:en:37:58).

quote: In the same year, many distinguished men strove for the censorship
notes: Violent nobiles-versus-new-man contest for the censorship, inflamed by Glabrio's largesses and prosecution, ends with Flamininus and Marcellus elected censors (livy:en:37:58).

quote: There were some who judged that the war was greater by fame than by real difficulty
notes: The senate votes Regillus a naval triumph and L. Scipio, now styling himself Asiaticus, a triumph, amid detractors belittling the Asian victory's difficulty (livy:en:37:59); coded electoral-conflict as nearest type for contested honors.
